mainTopic: Who must write the גט when a husband tells a group to write or give it, and שמואל's doubt about agents who had a סופר write it
overview: The amud finishes a משנה about a husband who tells a group of people to handle his גט. If he tells three people 'write and give,' they write it themselves. If he says only 'give,' רבי מאיר holds that he made them a בית דין, so they may have others write it. רבי יוסי reports a tradition that even the בית דין הגדול would have to learn to write and do it themselves. If he speaks to ten people, one writes and two sign, but if he says 'all of you,' everyone must sign. The גמרא then brings a question sent to שמואל about two agents who had a סופר write the גט. שמואל answered 'she must leave, and the matter requires study.' The גמרא works out that his doubt is whether 'write' means the agents' signatures or the text of the גט. It tests this against the משנה and against רבי יוסי's rule that spoken instructions cannot be passed on to an agent. The amud ends in the middle of a challenge about whether רבי יוסי accepts a husband who says 'tell someone.' That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Telling three people to write and give
steps.stepSummary: If a man tells three people 'Write a גט and give it to my wife,' they themselves write it and give it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if he said to three people: 'Write a גט and give it to my wife,' these people should write it and give it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of cases. When the husband clearly says 'write and give,' the people he spoke to must do both jobs themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband gave two clear instructions, writing and giving. The people he appointed carry out his exact words and do not pass the writing on to anyone else.

phrases.english: Or to three people:
'Write a bill of divorce, and give it to my wife,'
these people should write it and give it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ לִשְׁלֹשָׁה כִּתְבוּ גֵּט וּתְנוּ לְאִשְׁתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier part of the משנה, which comes before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An explicit instruction to write and give means the appointed people write and deliver the גט themselves.

steps.title: Telling three people only to give
steps.stepSummary: If he tells three people only 'Give a גט to my wife,' רבי מאיר says they may have others write it, because he made them a בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said to three people: 'Give a גט to my wife,' they should tell others to write it, because he made them a court. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the husband says only 'give' to three people. רבי מאיר rules that they may tell other people to write the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three people form a בית דין, and a בית דין can appoint others to act for it. Since the husband did not say 'write,' the three are not personally required to write. Acting as a court, they may instruct others to write it.

keyTerms.meaning: They tell others (to do the job)
Because he made them into a court
The תנא who gives this ruling

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In step 1 he said 'write and give,' so they must write it themselves. Here he said only 'give,' so they may have others write it.

phrases.english: If he said to three people:
'Give a bill of divorce to my wife,'
these people should tell others, and those others will write it,
because he made them a court;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 1. Here 'give' is said alone, without 'write.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, three people told only 'give' act as a בית דין and may tell others to write the גט.

steps.title: A received tradition supporting רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא איש אונו reports a tradition he brought out from prison that matches רבי מאיר's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the הלכה that רבי חנינא of Ono brought out from prison: 'I have received a tradition that if a man says to three people, "Give a גט to my wife," they should tell others to write it, because he made them a court.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up רבי מאיר's ruling. A sage reports that he received this exact law as a tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is not only רבי מאיר's own reasoning. It is a received tradition, carried by רבי חנינא איש אונו. Its wording matches step 2, including the reason that the three are a בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי חנינא from the town of Ono

phrases.english: And this is the halakha that was brought up by

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אִישׁ אוֹנוֹ מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִין:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina of Ono, from prison:
phrases.notes: He heard this teaching from someone held in prison and brought it out to share.

phrases.english: I have received a tradition about one who says to three people:
'Give a bill of divorce to my wife'
that they should tell others, and those others will write it,
because he made them a court.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזוֹ הֲלָכָה הֶעֱלָה רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אִישׁ אוֹנוֹ מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2 with a received tradition.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's ruling that three people told 'give' may have others write the גט.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The tradition of רבי חנינא איש אונו, brought out from prison.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's opposing tradition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says he received a different tradition: even the great בית דין in Jerusalem, if told 'give,' must learn to write and then write and give the גט themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: We said to the messenger: We too have received a tradition. Even if a man said to the בית דין הגדול in ירושלים, 'Give a גט to my wife,' they must learn how to write, then write it and give it themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the tradition in step 3. He says the people appointed must write the גט themselves, even if they are the greatest court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's view depends on the three being a בית דין that may pass the job to others. רבי יוסי rejects that idea. Even the highest court cannot pass the writing on to others. If its members do not know how to write a גט, they must learn first.

keyTerms.meaning: Messenger (here, the one who carried the tradition)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: three people told 'give' are a בית דין and may have others write. רבי יוסי: anyone told 'give,' even the סנהדרין, must write the גט personally, learning how if needed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
We said to the messenger:
phrases.notes: The 'messenger' is רבי חנינא איש אונו, who carried the tradition in the last step.

phrases.english: We too have received a tradition,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ אָמַר לְבֵית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם:
phrases.english: that even if he said to the Great Court in Jerusalem:
'Give a bill of divorce to my wife'
they should learn how to write, then write it and give it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי נוּמֵינוּ לַשָּׁלִיחַ אַף אָנוּ מְקוּבָּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the tradition of step 3 with an opposing tradition.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that a group told only 'give' may assign the writing to others.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being a בית דין does not let them pass the job on. The husband's appointees must write it themselves.

steps.title: Telling ten people to write and give
steps.stepSummary: If a man tells ten people 'Write and give a גט to my wife,' one writes it and two sign it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said to ten people: 'Write and give a גט to my wife,' one writes and two sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts a new case with a larger group. When he speaks to all ten in a general way, not all of them need to take part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט needs one writer and two witnesses to sign. Since the husband did not insist on everyone, the usual minimum from the group is enough.

phrases.english: If he said to ten people:
'Write and give a bill of divorce to my wife'
one writes, and two sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לַעֲשָׂרָה כִּתְבוּ וּתְנוּ גֵּט לְאִשְׁתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case about a larger group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A general instruction to ten people is fulfilled by one writer and two signing witnesses.

steps.title: 'All of you': everyone must sign
steps.stepSummary: If he says 'All of you write,' one writes and all of them sign. So if one of them dies, the גט cannot be done.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'All of you write,' one writes and all of them sign. Therefore, if one of them dies, this גט is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The husband now adds 'all of you.' Every person in the group must take part, and the משנה gives the result if one of them dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'all of you' makes everyone's involvement part of his instruction. The writing is still done by one person, but all must sign. If one dies, his instruction can no longer be carried out, so the גט is void.
steps.whatToRemember: The husband's exact words decide who must take part. 'Write and give' to ten means one writer and two signers. 'All of you' means all must sign, so if one dies the גט is void.

phrases.english: If he said, 'All of you write'
one writes, and all of them sign;
therefore, if one of them died,
this is a void bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 5. Adding 'all of you' changes who must take part.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When told 'all of you,' all must sign, and if one dies the גט is void.

steps.title: רב's students ask שמואל about agents who had a scribe write the divorce document
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא reports that רב's study hall sent שמואל a question. A man told two people 'Write and give a גט.' They had a סופר write it and they signed it. Is it valid?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: They sent a question from רב's study hall to שמואל: 'Let our teacher teach us. A man said to two people, "Write and give a גט to my wife." They told a סופר and he wrote it, and they signed it. What is the law?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a real question sent to שמואל about a husband's instruction to two people. This sets up שמואל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is like the one in the משנה, where the husband said 'write and give.' The new twist is that the two agents did not write the גט themselves. They handed the writing to a סופר and only signed it.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall of רב (here, his students)
Let our teacher teach us (a polite way to open a question)
Scribe, a professional writer of documents

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
They sent from the study hall of Rav to Shmuel:
Let our teacher teach us:
A man said to two people:
"Write and give a divorce document to my wife,"
and they told a scribe and he wrote it,
and they themselves signed it. What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ מִבֵּי רַב לִשְׁמוּאֵל יְלַמְּדֵנוּ רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a practical question tied to the משנה's case of 'write and give.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a גט valid if the agents told to 'write and give' had a סופר write it and only signed it themselves?

steps.title: שמואל answers that she must leave but the matter needs more study
steps.stepSummary: שמואל replies that if the woman remarried using this גט she must leave her new husband. He adds that the issue still needs study.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to them: 'She must leave, and the matter requires study.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a strict practical answer: we do not rely on this גט. He also admits he is not fully sure of the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'She must leave' means the גט is treated as possibly invalid, so a second marriage based on it cannot stand. 'Requires study' shows this is a doubt, not a firm ruling. That opens the question the גמרא asks next.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent back to them (his written reply)
The matter requires study, meaning it is still unclear

steps.confusionAlert: 'She must leave' does not mean the גט is definitely invalid. שמואל is being strict because he is unsure.

phrases.english: He sent to them: She must leave,
phrases.notes: He means that if she remarried on the basis of this גט, she must leave the second husband.

phrases.english: and the matter requires study.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לְהוּ תֵּצֵא וְהַדָּבָר צָרִיךְ תַּלְמוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question sent in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The woman must leave her second husband, but the underlying law is still in doubt.

steps.title: What is שמואל unsure about? Maybe whether spoken instructions can be passed on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'requires study' means. It suggests שמואל was unsure whether spoken instructions can be handed on from one agent to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'the matter requires study' mean? If you say it is because these are only spoken instructions, and he is unsure whether spoken instructions can be passed on to another agent or not...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly שמואל was unsure about and offers a first guess. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband handed his agents nothing physical. He only gave spoken instructions. The guess is that שמואל did not know whether agents who received only words may pass the job to someone else, here the סופר.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will usually be rejected)
Can be handed over to an agent

phrases.english: What does "the matter requires study" mean?
If you say it is because these are only words,
and he is unsure about words:
whether they can be handed over to an agent,
or whether they cannot be handed over to an agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind שמואל's doubt in step 8 and offers a first suggestion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly was שמואל unsure about?

steps.title: That can't be it, since שמואל already ruled like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. שמואל quoted רבי that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, who says spoken instructions cannot be passed on to an agent. So שמואל had no doubt about this.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't שמואל say in the name of רבי: The law follows רבי יוסי, who said spoken instructions cannot be handed over to an agent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the first guess by pointing to a clear ruling שמואל himself reported.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל already held, as רבי יוסי does, that spoken instructions cannot be passed on. If so, he should have called the גט plainly invalid, not said 'requires study.' His doubt must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (introduces a challenge from someone's own statement)
רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה

phrases.english: But didn't Shmuel say that Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: Plain 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: The law follows Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי from step 4, who says even the great בית דין must write and give the גט themselves.

phrases.english: who said words cannot be handed over to an agent!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר רַבִּי הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that שמואל was unsure whether spoken instructions can be passed on to an agent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל himself reported that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, who says spoken instructions cannot be passed on. So he had a clear position and no doubt on this point.

steps.title: שמואל's real doubt is what the husband meant by 'write'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that שמואל's doubt was about the word 'write.' Did the husband mean 'write your signatures' or 'write the גט itself'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what שמואל was unsure about: does this word 'write' mean the writing of their own hands (their signatures), or the writing of the divorce document?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true reason for שמואל's doubt. The question is about the meaning of the husband's words, not about passing on spoken instructions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'write' meant their signatures, they did exactly what was asked, and a סופר may write the text. If 'write' meant the text of the גט, they had to write it themselves, and handing it to a סופר would be passing on spoken instructions, which רבי יוסי forbids. Since the meaning is unclear, שמואל was strict and said 'she must leave.'

keyTerms.meaning: He is asking, it is a question for him
The writing of the גט's text

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל agrees with רבי יוסי that spoken instructions cannot be passed on. His only doubt is whether 'write' meant 'sign' or 'write the whole גט.' That doubt is why he said 'she must leave, and the matter requires study.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the meaning of a husband's exact words decides whether his agents may bring in a סופר.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לִשְׁמוּאֵל – הָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rather, for Shmuel, this is what he is asking:
this word "write":
does it mean the writing of their hands,
phrases.notes: Their signatures as witnesses. If so, a סופר could write the rest.

phrases.english: or the writing of the divorce document?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לִשְׁמוּאֵל הָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 10 rules out the first guess, gives the true source of שמואל's doubt.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the doubt: it is about the meaning of the husband's words, not the rule on passing on spoken instructions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל was unsure whether spoken instructions can be passed on to another agent.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל holds they cannot be passed on. He is unsure whether 'write' meant the signatures or the text of the גט.

steps.title: Why not settle the question from the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל was unsure, since the משנה says that people told 'write a גט and give it' must write it themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him settle the question from our משנה: If a man told two people 'Give a גט to my wife,' or told three people 'Write a גט and give it to my wife,' then these people should write it and give it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's doubt. It points to our משנה, which seems to answer the question already.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that when the husband said 'write,' the people he spoke to must write the גט themselves ('יכתבו ויתנו'). That seems to show 'write' means writing the actual גט. If so, having a סופר write it should clearly not work, and שמואל should not have needed to say 'it requires study.'

keyTerms.meaning: Let him resolve / settle the question
These people should write it and give it (themselves)

phrases.english: But let him resolve it from our משנה:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is שמואל, who said the case still needs study.

phrases.english: If he said to two: "Give a גט to my wife,"
or to three: "Write a גט and give it to my wife" —
these people should write and give it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the doubt described in step 11 (does 'write' mean the גט or the signatures) by citing the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that the case 'requires study'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules that those told 'write' must write the גט themselves. That seems to settle the meaning of 'write,' so there should be no doubt.

steps.title: The משנה's wording is itself the doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word 'write' in the משנה is exactly what שמואל was unsure about: signatures or the גט itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: That very משנה is what he is unsure about: does 'write' mean writing their signatures, or writing the גט?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The משנה cannot settle the doubt, because the same unclear word 'write' appears in the משנה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'write,' but it never says what to write. If 'write' means 'sign as witnesses,' then the משנה does not rule out a סופר writing the text. So שמואל's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: That very thing is what he is asking about
Their own handwriting, meaning their signatures
Writing the text of the גט itself

phrases.english: That very משנה is what he is unsure about:
"Write" — does it mean their signatures,
or does it mean writing the גט?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by showing that the משנה contains the same unclear word.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The source is shown to be unclear in the same way as the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה clearly means the agents write the גט themselves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's 'write' could mean only signatures, so it does not settle שמואל's doubt.

steps.title: Proof from רבי יוסי's statement about the Great Court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues it is obvious that 'write' means the גט, since the משנה says even the בית דין הגדול must 'learn' to write, and judges surely know how to sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that it means writing the גט, because the later part of the משנה teaches: רבי יוסי said, 'We told the messenger: We too have a tradition that even if a man told the בית דין הגדול in ירושלים "Give a גט to my wife," they must learn, write, and give it to her.' If 'write' means the גט, that makes sense. But if it means signatures, is there any court whose members don't know how to sign their names?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the doubt again. It brings proof from the end of the משנה that 'write' must mean writing the actual גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says even the greatest court must 'learn' and then write. Learning makes sense for writing a גט, which takes real skill. It makes no sense for signing, because every judge already knows how to sign his own name.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה
The Great Court (the סנהדרין) in ירושלים

phrases.english: It is obvious that it means writing the גט,
as the later part of the משנה teaches:
רבי יוסי said: We said to the messenger:
We too have received a tradition

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ אָמַר לְבֵית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם:
phrases.english: that even if he said to the Great Court in ירושלים:
"Give a גט to my wife" —
they should learn, and write, and give it to her.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא כְּתַב הַגֵּט הוּא, שַׁפִּיר;
phrases.english: Granted, if you say it means writing the גט, that works well;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ כְּתַב יָדָן הוּא,
phrases.english: but if you say it means their signatures,
is there any court
whose members do not know how to sign their own signatures?!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא דִּכְתַב הַגֵּט הוּא, דְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 13 by using the end of the same משנה to show that 'write' is not unclear.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 13 that 'write' might mean only signatures
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires the court to 'learn' before writing. Judges never need to learn how to sign, so 'write' must mean writing the גט.

steps.title: A new court might need to learn to sign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a newly formed court may not yet have practiced signatures, so 'learn' could still refer to signing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, there is such a court: a new court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The word 'learn' could fit signatures after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Members of a brand-new court may not yet have a settled, recognizable signature. So 'learn and write' could mean learning to sign properly. That keeps open the possibility that 'write' means signatures, and שמואל's doubt survives.

phrases.english: Yes, there is: a new court.
phrases.notes: He means judges who have not yet practiced a set signature that people would recognize.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects the proof in step 14 by describing a case where 'learning' fits signatures.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: a new court that still needs to practice signing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No court would ever need to learn how to sign, so 'write' must mean the גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: A new court might need to learn signing, so the משנה does not prove anything, and the doubt stands.

steps.title: Even if 'write' means sign, a סופר still should not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even if 'write' means signatures, how could a סופר's writing of the גט be valid, when the הלכה follows רבי יוסי that spoken instructions cannot be handed to an agent?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we hold that this 'write' means their signatures, is the writing of the גט by a סופר then valid?! But שמואל said in the name of רבי: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, who says spoken instructions cannot be handed on to an agent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. Even if 'write' means only signing, there still seems to be a problem with the סופר writing the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'write' means 'sign,' then the husband never told the two men to arrange for the גט to be written. By having a סופר write it, they passed his spoken instructions on to another agent. שמואל himself rules like רבי יוסי that this cannot be done, so why would he have any doubt about the case?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say…? (introduces a contradiction)
Spoken instructions cannot be handed on to an agent

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same rule of רבי יוסי from step 10. There it was used to reject one explanation of שמואל's doubt. Here it is used against the new explanation (signatures versus the גט).

phrases.english: And if we hold
that this "write" means their signatures,
is the writing of the גט then valid?!
But didn't שמואל say in the name of רבי:
The הלכה follows רבי יוסי,
who says spoken instructions cannot be handed on to an agent!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סְבִירָא לַן דְּהַאי ״כְּתוֹבוּ״ – כְּתַב יָדָן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 15 keeps the 'signatures' reading alive, this step attacks that reading using the rule of רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation from step 11 that שמואל's doubt was about the meaning of 'write'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'write' means only signatures, the סופר's writing was never authorized, so the agents passed on spoken instructions. רבי יוסי, whom שמואל follows, invalidates that. So there should be no doubt at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge shows that changing what the doubt is about does not, on its own, escape רבי יוסי's rule. The next step gives the further answer that explains שמואל's 'requires study.'

steps.title: Writing the גט counts as 'Tell someone,' which רבי יוסי accepts
steps.stepSummary: If 'write' means signatures, then having the סופר write the גט is like the husband saying 'tell someone,' and רבי יוסי agrees to that.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: if we hold that 'write' means their own signatures, then the writing of the גט itself is treated as if the husband said 'Tell someone to write it.' And רבי יוסי agrees in a case where the husband says 'Tell.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 16. It explains how a סופר can validly write the גט if the people were only told to sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's rule is that spoken instructions cannot be passed on to another agent. But when the husband himself says 'Tell someone,' the agent is not passing on his own job. He is carrying out exactly what the husband asked for. So the writing of the גט is treated as that kind of case, and רבי יוסי has no problem with it.

keyTerms.meaning: They say. It introduces an answer from the scholars.
'Say!' The husband tells the agents to instruct someone else.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In 'מילי לא מימסרן לשליח,' the agent passes his own job to someone else on his own initiative, and that doesn't work. In 'אמרו,' the husband himself asks the agent to tell someone else, and רבי יוסי agrees that this works.

phrases.english: They say: if we hold
that 'write' refers to their handwriting,
phrases.notes: Their handwriting means their signatures as witnesses, not the text of the גט.

phrases.english: then the writing of the גט becomes like one who says: 'Tell',
and רבי יוסי agrees in the case of one who says 'Tell.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 16 based on רבי יוסי's rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the case as 'אמרו,' which רבי יוסי accepts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Having a סופר write the גט means the agents passed on their spoken job, which רבי יוסי forbids
steps.terutzMaskana: The writing is treated as if the husband said 'Tell someone,' which רבי יוסי allows

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה of a scribe and one witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא doubts that רבי יוסי agrees to 'Tell.' It brings a משנה about a scribe and one witness, which רב חסדא says follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רבי יוסי really agree when one says 'Tell'? Didn't we learn: 'If a scribe wrote and there is one witness, the גט is valid'? And רבי ירמיה said: we learned this about the scribe's signature. And רב חסדא said: whose view is this משנה? It is רבי יוסי's, who said that spoken instructions cannot be handed to an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer from Step 17. It sets up a source to show that רבי יוסי may not accept 'Tell someone' after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה accepts a גט signed by the scribe together with one other witness. רב חסדא explains that this follows רבי יוסי: since instructions can't be passed to an agent, we don't worry that the scribe signed without the husband's own order. The next step shows why this clashes with the claim that רבי יוסי accepts 'אמרו.'

keyTerms.meaning: And is it really so? It opens a challenge.
But didn't we learn in a משנה?
Spoken instructions cannot be handed over to another agent

phrases.english: But does רבי יוסי really agree
in the case of one who says: 'Tell'?!
But didn't we learn: 'A scribe wrote, and a witness — it is valid'?
phrases.notes: This is a different משנה, later in this מסכת. The scribe plus one other witness count as the two witnesses.

phrases.english: And רבי ירמיה said: we learned 'the scribe signed';
And רב חסדא said: whose view is the משנה?
It is רבי יוסי's, who said:
spoken instructions cannot be handed to an agent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּאוֹמֵר: ״אִמְרוּ״?! וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in Step 17 that רבי יוסי agrees to 'אמרו'
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי agrees when the husband says 'אמרו'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה that רב חסדא assigns to רבי יוסי seems to depend on agents never being able to bring in someone else, which suggests רבי יוסי does not accept 'אמרו'

steps.title: If רבי יוסי accepts 'Tell,' a problem follows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to show that if רבי יוסי accepted 'Tell,' the משנה of the scribe and one witness would lead to a bad result.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that רבי יוסי agrees when one says 'Tell,' a pitfall comes out of it. Because sometimes the husband said to two people:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its challenge and begins to describe a problem case. The sentence continues on the next amud, where the details of the case are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'אמרו' worked for רבי יוסי, we could no longer be sure the scribe signed on the husband's own order. The husband might have spoken to two other people, who then brought in the scribe. So the משנה's simple acceptance of the scribe and one witness could lead to an invalid גט being treated as valid.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (if you thought)
A pitfall (a bad result) comes out of it

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that רבי יוסי agrees in the case of one who says 'Tell',
a pitfall comes out of it,
for sometimes he said to two people:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּאוֹמֵר ״אִמְרוּ״, נָפֵיק מִינַּהּ חוּרְבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the source in Step 18 contradicts Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 17 that רבי יוסי agrees to 'אמרו'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'אמרו' worked for רבי יוסי, the scribe might have signed because of intermediaries rather than the husband himself, so the משנה could not simply call the גט valid
